title: Foundations of GenIR
extended_summary: This chapter provides a conceptual overview of generative AI for information access (IA), focusing on how modern generative models change retrieval and synthesis systems. It argues that generative AI creates two major new paradigms: information generation, where models directly produce tailored content for a user’s need, and information synthesis, where models integrate external information to generate grounded responses. The paper positions these developments as foundational for future IA systems rather than reporting an empirical study.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/chapter-style review of generative AI and information access, not an empirical study. It contains no original evaluation design, sample, or measured outcomes relevant to K-12 science learning.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports no direct educational intervention effects and no K-12 science learning outcomes. Any implications for education are indirect and speculative rather than evidentiary.

interventions.use_case: Conceptual discussion of large language models and chatbots (e.g., ChatGPT) as information-generating and information-synthesizing systems, including retrieval-augmented generation and prompt optimization for direct answers.
Retrieval-augmented generation and generative retrieval as information-access architectures that combine retrieval systems with generative models for grounded response synthesis.
